summary: The reference implements rules 2-7 faithfully. Its rule-1 clock handling is incomplete for contract-valid inputs the sealed generator deliberately avoids. (1) Year inference goes wrong when a backward clock step straddles a month boundary. (2) Non-auth host-clock records (wtmp logins/logouts, btmp, ctimes, dpkg, history stamps) are placed on a side of the step using only an auth-log-derived host-time threshold, which misplaces collector-settleable logins in a backward-step overlap and misses a step whose pre-step auth lines were rotated away. Both are narrow boundary defects, so each is rated Minor.

unread_or_truncated_ranges: environment/app/evidence/case-1/var/log/wtmp, var/log/btmp (binary; string fields visible, int32 times not decodable without a shell), var/log/auth.log.2.gz and auth.log.3.gz (gzip) are opaque case-1 fixtures. No report is supplied for case-1, and the reference's parsing of these formats was checked against record-formats.md instead, so they are not needed for this axis.

findings.claim: date_lines() assigns auth-log years by decrementing whenever a line's month exceeds the next line's month in file order. After a backward clock step (host clock ahead, then set back) that straddles a month boundary, the non-monotonic host month is read as a year rollover. Every earlier auth line is then dated one year too early, and the derived step offset becomes about one year, which fix() applies to every pre-step wtmp/btmp/ctime/dpkg/history time.

finding_evidence.expected_behavior: case-guide.md rule 1: report true UTC times for a host clock that may have been wrong by a fixed amount for part of the period and then set right once. instruction.md allows a step of 30-7200 s, any year 2019-2031 and collections crossing December into January. Nothing excludes a step near a month end, so pre-step records must be reported at their true times.
finding_evidence.actual_behavior: Pre-step auth lines get year Y-1. d = true - t becomes about 365 days - n, so step_n is about 1 year - n. fix() adds that to every host-clock record below step_t, and pre-step logins, failures and ctimes are reported about one year late.
finding_evidence.trace_or_receipt: Offset +00:00. Clock ahead by n=900 s until true tc=2025-03-31T23:55:00Z. A collector-kept sshd line at true 23:54:59 is written 'Apr  1 00:09:59', and the next line, at true 23:55:00, is written 'Mar 31 23:55:00'. solution/triage.py:72-74 walks backward: at i=the Apr line, parsed[i][0]=4 > parsed[i+1][0]=3, so year becomes 2024 for it and all earlier lines. solution/triage.py:124-128 sets step_n = true - t = 31536000-900 for those lines. solution/triage.py:129-130 sets step_t at the first agreeing line (host 2025-03-31T23:55:00). solution/triage.py:132-133 then adds about 1 year to every wtmp/btmp/ctime/dpkg/history time below step_t, so a pre-step intruder login on 2025-03-20 is reported as about 2026-03-20. Static trace, not executed.

findings.reachable_case_or_path: Any evidence directory with a backward clock step whose true time tc lies within n seconds before a month boundary, with an auth-log line recorded in [boundary - n, tc). The Dec->Jan case is explicitly in the instruction's domain. solution/model.py:425 (a.month == b.month) shows that the sealed generator never emits this case.
findings.graded_effect: initial_access.time, first_activity, last_activity, privilege_escalation (sudo lines no longer fall inside the shifted sessions) and persistence membership (ctime windows) can all be wrong for such a directory. The current sealed corpus avoids the case, so Oracle reward is unaffected. The reference still fails 'every rule in the guide holds for every such directory'.
findings.root_invariant: Auth-log year assignment must follow true chronology, not host-clock month order, which a backward step can make non-monotonic.
sibling_variants: Backward step straddling Dec 31 -> Jan 1 (the year-crossing family combined with the clock family): same decrement at the Jan->Dec host order, so pre-step lines lose a year.
Forward step (host clock behind) across a month boundary keeps host months monotonic and is handled correctly. This was checked and is not a sibling defect.
interaction_variants: Rule 1 x rule 3: pre-step wtmp logins are shifted about +1 year by fix(), so the earliest hostile login and its time are wrong.
Rule 1 x rule 6: ctimes below step_t are shifted out of every intruder window, so persistence is dropped.
findings.minimal_repair_boundary: date_lines() year assignment: anchor each line's year using the collector copies or the step detection (for example treat a small backward jump as a clock step rather than a year rollover), or compute years after the step correction.
closure_evidence: A generated case with a backward step of 900 s placed 300 s before a month end, and one before Jan 1, where the reference output equals model truth.
A mutant that ignores the step still fails those cases.

findings.claim: For every host-clock record that is not an auth-log line, the reference decides the side of the step with one host-time threshold (t < step_t), and it derives the step only from auth-log lines paired with collector lines. The guide promises the collector settles each graded time's side, and two collector-settleable cases break this: (a) after a backward step, an intruder login/logout whose true time is within n seconds before the step has a host time >= step_t and is left uncorrected, although its Accepted/session-closed sshd line in the collector log settles it as pre-step; (b) when rotation removed every pre-step auth line, no auth line disagrees with the collector, so step_n stays 0 and pre-step wtmp/btmp/ctime records are never corrected, although collector Accepted lines versus wtmp logins still show the offset.

finding_evidence.expected_behavior: case-guide.md rule 1: report true times, and 'The collector's record always settles which side of a step every graded host-clock time lies on.' record-formats.md: the collector keeps every non-failure sshd line for the whole evidence period, including Accepted and session-closed lines in the same second they were written. A login in the backward-step overlap, or before a step whose auth lines were rotated away, is therefore settled by the collector, and the report must use its true time.
finding_evidence.actual_behavior: (a) The login is reported n seconds late. (b) Pre-step failures and logins are reported N seconds off.
finding_evidence.trace_or_receipt: (a) Backward step n=600 at true tc, initial login at true tc-100. The host wrote wtmp tv_sec=tc+500. The first agreeing auth line has host time tc, so step_t=tc (solution/triage.py:129-130). fix(tc+500) is not < step_t, so it returns tc+500 (solution/triage.py:132-133, 137). initial_access.time is tc+500 instead of tc-100, although the collector holds 'Accepted ... for USER from ADDR' at tc-100. (b) Clock behind by N until tc, auth.log rotation keeps only lines after tc, and the intruder's earlier failures (btmp) and admin logins precede tc. solution/triage.py:124-130 iterates only `dated` auth lines, every d==0, step_t stays None, and fix() is the identity. btmp failures of the intruder address are reported N seconds early, and first_activity is wrong by N. The reference's own solve.sh:10 comment admits the assumption: 'no graded record falls where host times overlap after a backward step'. The candidate-visible contract states no such restriction. Static trace, not executed.

findings.reachable_case_or_path: (a) A backward step of 30-7200 s placed within n seconds after an intruder login or logout, allowed by instruction.md:5 and case-guide rule 1. solution/model.py:402-413 and 425 exclude it from the sealed corpus. (b) A forward or backward step that precedes the oldest retained auth-log line while graded host-clock records (intruder failures days earlier, logins) precede the step. instruction.md:5 allows rotation and a step independently, and case-guide.md:17-19 anticipates rotation eating into the intruder's failures.
findings.graded_effect: initial_access.time, first_activity and last_activity can be wrong by the step size. Session windows shift too, which can move sudo attribution (privilege_escalation) and persistence ctime membership. The sealed corpus avoids these layouts, so Oracle reward is unaffected, but the reference disagrees with the guide on contract-valid directories.
findings.root_invariant: Every graded host-clock record must be placed on the side of the step that the collector's record establishes, and the step must be found from all collector-settleable evidence, not only from surviving local auth-log lines and one host-time cutoff.
sibling_variants: wtmp logout (DEAD_PROCESS) in the backward-step overlap: its sshd 'session closed' line is collector-kept, so it is settleable but misplaced the same way.
Auth-log lines themselves are handled correctly by file order (step_i). This was checked and is not a sibling.
btmp failures, ctimes and history stamps in the overlap cannot be settled by the collector, so the guide's promise excludes them. They are not claimed here.
interaction_variants: Rule 1 x rule 5: a shifted session window can exclude or include a sudo line on that TTY via session_at (solution/triage.py:172-176).
Rule 1 x rule 7: an open final session's uncorrected start or a pre-step failure changes first_activity or last_activity.
Rule 1 x auth-log rotation (rule 2 context): case (b).
findings.minimal_repair_boundary: The rule-1 correction layer: pair wtmp logins and logouts with collector Accepted/session-closed lines to find and bound the step and to settle overlap records, and use auth-log/collector pairs only as one source of that evidence.
closure_evidence: A generated backward-step case with the initial login 100 s before tc where the reference matches truth.
A generated forward-step case with the rotation cut after tc and intruder failures before tc where the reference matches truth.
An existing sealed corpus that still passes.

checks_performed: Traced read_collection sign and offset parsing and epoch() local->UTC conversion for negative and positive offsets (case-1 -12:00: auth.log 'Jan  2 21:17:07' maps to 2022-01-03T09:17:07Z, which matches remote/files.log:58).
Traced auth_lines rotation ordering (highest number first, .gz decompress) against record-formats.md:9-13.
Traced date_lines year inference for the last line against collected_utc, for a Dec->Jan crossing without a step, for a forward step across a month, and for a backward step across a month (CRS-1).
Traced the step detection loop and fix() for a forward step (no overlap, correct), for a backward step (CRS-2a) and for a step before the retained auth lines (CRS-2b).
Checked rule 2 hostile detection (btmp type 6, sliding five-failure window <=600 s inclusive).
Checked rule 3 (earliest wtmp USER_PROCESS from a hostile host).

Checked the rule 4 fixed point: key extraction from histories of intruder accounts including root after escalation, fingerprint computation matching record-formats.md:42-45, key-login address expansion, no password tie.
Checked rule 5: sudo USER=root on a TTY whose covering wtmp session is an intruder session, or an intruder root login, whichever is earlier.

Checked rule 6: path kinds (cron.d, crontabs, systemd .service/.timer below /etc/systemd/system including *.wants, rc.local, authorized_keys regex), ctime used rather than mtime, dpkg exclusion |ctime - installed| <= 2 inclusive with arch-suffixed .list names.

Checked rule 7 event set: intruder-source failures, logins/logouts, TTY-tied sudo lines, persistence ctimes, stamped history inside intruder windows. An open session's end is excluded as an event, and collected_utc is used only as a window bound.
Checked the report shape against report.md: seven keys, ISO-Z times, null privilege_escalation, sets.
Checked operating constraints: stdlib only, read-only evidence, optional directories absent, no dependency on /app/evidence.

coverage_sweep.category: Trace an ordinary case and each relevant boundary through the reference logic
coverage_sweep.reason: Traced case-1 shaped inputs through every rule. Boundaries traced: 600 s inclusive window, 2 s dpkg inclusive, session window inclusive, open session, Dec->Jan year crossing, forward and backward clock step. Defects appear only on the backward-step month boundary and on collector-settleable records outside the auth-derived threshold.

coverage_sweep.category: Output bytes: widths, precision, delimiters, paths
coverage_sweep.reason: iso() emits YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ in UTC. The keys match report.md exactly. Lists are sorted unique sets, and null is emitted for no escalation.

coverage_sweep.category: Every branch that updates state (identifier reuse, replacement, expiry)
coverage_sweep.reason: wtmp session pairing by tty with pop on logout handles tty reuse. The fixed-point loop recomputes pe and accounts each iteration until stable. The persistence dict is keyed by path. Remote true_at is keyed by 'sshd[pid]: msg', and pid reuse with an identical message is theoretically possible but speculative, so it is not claimed.

coverage_sweep.category: Recovery and durability at interruption points
coverage_sweep.reason: A single-shot read-only analyzer that writes one JSON file, with no recovery contract.

coverage_sweep.category: Rule 1 time handling (UTC offset, year inference, clock step)
coverage_sweep.reason: Offset handling is correct. Year inference fails on a backward step across a month (CRS-1). Side assignment for non-auth records relies on an auth-derived threshold (CRS-2).

Each rule is implemented as the guide states (see checks_performed). No independent defect was found. Attributing concurrent admin root-history commands or admin file edits inside an intruder window is a contract-determinacy question for coherent_contract, not a reference defect.

coverage_sweep.category: solve.sh installs the reference at the declared path
coverage_sweep.reason: It copies solution/triage.py to /app/triage.py with mode 0755. The comment map matches the implementation.

interaction_sweep.case_or_path: Backward step of 900 s at 5 minutes before a month end: host month order goes 4 then 3.
Backward step 100 s after the initial login: the wtmp host time exceeds step_t, so it is left uncorrected.
Step before the oldest retained auth line: no disagreeing pair, so step_n=0.
The intruder adds a key to /root/.ssh/authorized_keys and logs in as root from new address B. The fixed point adds B, marks the root session, and sets pe to the earlier of sudo and root login.
The dpkg local time and the listed file ctime are both passed through fix() before the 2 s comparison, so they stay consistent on the same side of a forward step.
The open session window extends to collected_utc only for membership, and the session end is not added as an event.
An admin sudo on its own pts while the intruder is logged in: session_at resolves to the admin session, which is excluded.
